english: 87-91. “O holy lord, are you (the Sage) Sayugvā named Raikva?”[1] On hearing his words the sage replied: “I surely am Sayugvā named Raikva.” He heard the words of the sage. english: Moreover, the cognition of a word is not that of a partless whole. But it is an ideal construction of a series of consecutive letters since the hypothesis that a word consists of no parts has been refuted. We should also remember in this connection that two or three, or three or four, or five or six letters constitute a word, these letters are consecutively presented to our cons- ciousness, and the consciousness of each letter comes into being and passes away in a consecutive order. All the letters which constitute a word are never simultaneously presented to our consciousness. The cognition of the last word turns up in this way.
